title: Case: Rural recipient cannot find a parcel that the tracker and a delivery photo show as delivered
context: Tallowmere Goods order TG-941 (a box of drip-irrigation fittings) travelled as DL-941 to a rural address. The recipient account and shipment match are verified.
initial_request: I have now been sent a photograph of a box on some grass next to a fence and told the matter is closed. I have about four miles of fence and a good deal of grass. The photo is not of my garden, or not any part of it I recognise, and there is no 'rear of property' here that a van can reach. Last time I found the parcel myself after two days by walking the track across the marsh. I would rather not make that a habit. Could somebody find out where the driver actually put it.

events.body: DL-941 (Tallowmere order TG-941) displays delivered at 13:48 UTC today. Delivery photo on file: a brown carton on rough grass beside a wire fence. No building, door, gate or house number is in frame. No safe-place instruction is recorded for this address. We have not reviewed the route stop or the GPS point of the scan.

Tracker says delivered. It is not at the house, the porch, the log store or the gate. For the record this is the third one since February. The first went over the hedge into the lane. The second was on the lawn of the farm a quarter of a mile down. I have never set a safe place. Where is it this time?

Thank you for contacting Plover Arc. Our records show DL-941 was delivered at 13:48 with photographic proof of delivery. Please check your safe place and with your neighbours. This enquiry is now closed.

DL-941 driver note reads 'left safe place rear of property'. Driver is off shift until 06:00 tomorrow so we can't ask him where exactly, and the note doesn't say which property. Stop reviews and GPS pulls aren't ours, they sit with Delivery investigations, Plover Arc Logistics, by email.

I have now been sent a photograph of a box on some grass next to a fence and told the matter is closed. I have about four miles of fence and a good deal of grass. The photo is not of my garden, or not any part of it I recognise, and there is no 'rear of property' here that a van can reach. Last time I found the parcel myself after two days by walking the track across the marsh. I would rather not make that a habit. Could somebody find out where the driver actually put it.

acceptable_actions.summary: Open a delivery investigation on DL-941: delivered scan and photo versus the recipient's report, with a request to pull the GPS point and review the stop.

must: Sets out both sides of the conflict without choosing one: the 13:48 delivered scan, photo and driver note 'left safe place rear of property' against the recipient's report that the parcel is not at the address and the photo is not a place he recognises.
Asks for the route stop and GPS point of the scan to be reviewed, noting that no safe-place instruction is on file and the photo shows no identifiable building or number.

Tells the investigations team this is the recipient's third parcel since February left in an unrecorded spot and that Customer care has already closed his enquiry on the photo, so they can prioritise it.
must_not: Cites the delivery photo or the delivered scan as proof of delivery, or treats the case as closed.
Tells the recipient to keep searching his land, check the safe place or ask neighbours as the answer to his message.
States that the parcel is lost, was misdelivered to another property, or that the driver falsified the delivery.
Promises a replacement, refund, compensation or a recovery time.
expected.reference_message: Please open a delivery investigation for DL-941 (Tallowmere order TG-941). Tracking shows delivered at 13:48 UTC today with a photo of a carton on rough grass beside a wire fence; no building, gate or number is in frame. The driver note reads 'left safe place rear of property', but no safe-place instruction is on file for this address. The verified recipient, Oswin Tarrow, reports the parcel is not at the house, porch, log store or gate, does not recognise the place in the photo, and says there is no rear access a van can reach. Neither account is confirmed. Please pull the GPS point of the 13:48 scan and review the route stop; the driver is off shift until 06:00 tomorrow. For priority: this is the third parcel since February he reports being left in an unrecorded spot (over a hedge, on a neighbouring farm's lawn), and Customer care closed his enquiry today on the strength of the photo. Please send me a case reference and when to expect the next update. I am not treating this as a confirmed loss or misdelivery.

rationale: The scan, photo and driver note say delivered; the recipient says it is not there, and the photo cannot place the parcel at his address. Neither side is proven, and Dispatch has said the stop review belongs to Delivery investigations. The desk sends them the conflict and the repeat pattern rather than leaning on the photo as Customer care did.

review.note: Coordinator emailed Delivery investigations with both sides of the conflict, the GPS and stop-review request and the repeat pattern, matching the key.
